lessons.text: No word sheet for this step was found in the transcribed classes. He reads the Hebrew aloud with the class in the recording; his dictated explanation is below.
lessons.expl:
1Statementnumbering restartsWestwood · Nov 28, 2011 · 27:13
The Gemara now attempts to clarify the exact case over which Abaye/Rava are arguing.
The Gemara says that in a case where the object that was found had a sign on it, everyone would agree that the finder may not keep it.
Even if we find out that the owner later gave up hope, still the finder may not keep it.
This is because that since the object has a sign we must assume that its owner will not give up hope.
Therefore when the finder finds it, he must return it.
And, therefore, even if the owner gives up hope in the end, it will not take off the obligation to return it.

14QuestionWestwood · Jan 2, 2012 · 22:23
① The Torah designates that leket may be taken by the poor people.
② Gemara now brings a Mishnah regarding leket to attempt to resolve the dispute between Abaye and Rava.
③:
Ⓐ When is it that any person, rich or poor, is permitted to take the leket?
Ⓑ The Mishnah answers. After the namoshos have gone through the field.
④ The Gemara asks: what are namoshos?
⑤ The Gemara brings a dispute between Rabbi Yochanan and Reish Lakish.
⑥ Rabbi Yochanan:
He holds, it is the old men that go through the field. With their sticks,
⑦ Reish Lakish:
He holds. It is the second wave of poor that go through the field.
⑧ The Gemara now asks:
really? Leket is designated for all poor people worldwide.
⑨ Even if the local poor give up hope after the Namoshos go through the field. The distant poor have not given up hope.
since they are not even aware of the Namoshos.
⑩ yet still, the Mishnah says. That everyone may take the Leket, after the Namoshos went through the field.
⑪ the reason can only be because we assume that when the distant poor would find out about the Namoshos, they would surely give up hope.
⑫ This is a proof to Rava and a question on Abaye.

14QuestionWestwood · Jan 2, 2012 · 22:23
① The Torah designates that leket may be taken by the poor people.
② Gemara now brings a Mishnah regarding leket to attempt to resolve the dispute between Abaye and Rava.
③:
Ⓐ When is it that any person, rich or poor, is permitted to take the leket?
Ⓑ The Mishnah answers. After the namoshos have gone through the field.
④ The Gemara asks: what are namoshos?
⑤ The Gemara brings a dispute between Rabbi Yochanan and Reish Lakish.
⑥ Rabbi Yochanan:
He holds, it is the old men that go through the field. With their sticks,
⑦ Reish Lakish:
He holds. It is the second wave of poor that go through the field.
⑧ The Gemara now asks:
really? Leket is designated for all poor people worldwide.
⑨ Even if the local poor give up hope after the Namoshos go through the field. The distant poor have not given up hope.
since they are not even aware of the Namoshos.
⑩ yet still, the Mishnah says. That everyone may take the Leket, after the Namoshos went through the field.
⑪ the reason can only be because we assume that when the distant poor would find out about the Namoshos, they would surely give up hope.
⑫ This is a proof to Rava and a question on Abaye.

lessons.expl:
22QuestionWestwood · Jan 23, 2012 · 28:39
① The Gemara now brings a Braisa to try and resolve the dispute between Rava and Abaye.
② The Braisa says.
Ⅰ The case:
Ⓐ A secret thief stole from someone and gave it to another person.
Ⓑ An open thief stole from someone and gave it to another person.
Ⓒ The Jordan River took something from someone and deposited it by another person.
Ⅱ The halacha:
In all three cases, the person who received it may keep it.
③ The Gemara says that in the cases of:
Ⓐ the open thief
Ⓑ and the Jordan River.
the original owner is immediately aware of his loss, and he gives up hope right away.
④
But, by the case of the secret thief, when the person who received it got it, the owner was not yet aware of his loss.
⑤ Yet, still, the Braisa says that he may keep it.
⑥ The reason must be because when the owner discovers his loss, he will surely give up hope.
⑦ So, we see from here that potential giving up hope is enough.
⑧ Therefore, this Braisa is:
Ⓐ a proof for Rava,
Ⓑ and a proof against Abaye.
